Time-based Media Scenarios (WCAG 2.2: 1.2.1–1.2.5 focused fixture)
Purpose: provide a single HTML page containing many markup patterns a scanner might encounter for transcripts/captions and media alternatives. Some cases are intentionally ambiguous to force cantTell.

How to use this fixture

Each scenario is designed to exercise a specific detection/evaluation branch for time-based media rules. The Expected box is a human note suggesting what a strict deterministic engine might return (e.g., pass, informative, cantTell, or fail) for SC 1.2.1/1.2.2 depending on the evidence available.

Evidence types represented

  • Native <audio> and <video>
  • <track kind="captions"> (and related patterns)
  • Transcript as adjacent text section
  • Transcript link with explicit label (“Transcript”)
  • Transcript bound with aria-describedby
  • Transcript hidden/collapsed (details, CSS)
  • Transcript “elsewhere” (same-document anchor and cross-document href)
  • Multiple media items sharing one transcript
  • Ambiguous/misleading labels (forces cantTell)
  • Embedded players via <iframe>

Non-goals

  • Real playback (sources are placeholders and may not load)
  • Visual verification of captions rendering/quality
  • Provider-specific player APIs (YouTube/Vimeo caption state, etc.)

Tip: where you cannot prove compliance from the evidence, return cantTell rather than guessing.

S00No time-based media on page

Baseline: nothing to detect.

Expected: Inventory rule: pass. 1.2.1/1.2.2: notApplicable.

S01Audio-only with adjacent transcript section (explicit heading)

Native audio followed by visible transcript with “Transcript” heading.

Transcript

[Transcript text] Speaker: Welcome to the audio-only clip. This is a placeholder transcript.

Expected: 1.2.1: likely pass (strong transcript evidence).

S02Audio-only with transcript link (explicit label)

Transcript is elsewhere but clearly labeled.

Transcript

Expected: 1.2.1: likely pass if same-document anchors are accepted as transcript locations.

S03Audio-only with nearby text but no transcript labeling

Text could be a summary, not clearly a transcript.

This audio discusses product updates and includes several interview excerpts.

Expected: 1.2.1: cantTell (not clearly a transcript).

S04Audio-only with transcript hidden via details

Transcript is present but collapsed by default.

Transcript

[Transcript text] This transcript is inside a collapsed disclosure.

Expected: 1.2.1: pass or cantTell depending on your policy about collapsed content discoverability.

S05Video-only signal (muted) with transcript

Video is muted (attempting “video-only”). Transcript is clearly provided.

Transcript

[Transcript text] A silent animation shows a workflow diagram progressing through stages.

Expected: 1.2.1: likely pass for video-only media alternative (if muted is accepted as strong signal).

S06Video with captions track present

Native video includes a captions track.

Expected: 1.2.2: could be informative pass (captions track present). Audio presence may still be cantTell if you require proof.

S07Video without captions track

Native video has no <track kind="captions">.

Expected: 1.2.2: usually cantTell (cannot prove audio exists). Some tools emit an informative warning.

S08Video with “subtitles” track (not captions)

Track kind is subtitles, not captions.

Expected: 1.2.2: cantTell or informative (subtitles may not capture non-dialog audio cues).

S09Video with multiple caption tracks (no default)

Multiple caption tracks; default not set.

Expected: 1.2.2: likely informative pass (captions available), depending on your policy.

S10Transcript referenced via aria-describedby

Transcript is a plain div; media references it via describedby.

Transcript: [Transcript text] This audio introduces the quarterly report.

Expected: 1.2.1: likely pass (strong binding).

S11Transcript exists but is display:none

Transcript is in markup but hidden from all users.

Transcript

[Transcript text] Hidden transcript that users cannot access.

Expected: Policy-sensitive: cantTell or fail depending on whether hidden alternatives count as “provided”.

S12Transcript link present but label is ambiguous (“Read more”)

Transcript exists but link text doesn’t indicate transcript.

Read more

Expected: 1.2.1: cantTell (cannot confirm link is transcript).

S13Multiple audio clips sharing one transcript section

One transcript covers multiple clips.

Transcript

[Transcript text] This transcript covers both clips: part 1 and part 2.

Expected: 1.2.1: likely pass for both if describedby association is accepted.

S14Transcript present but extremely short (likely summary)

Tests any “minimum transcript length” guardrail you might use.

Transcript: Hello.

Expected: Conservative engines often choose cantTell (insufficient evidence) to avoid false passes.

S15Embedded player iframe (unknown captions/transcript)

Common in the wild; markup alone rarely proves captions/transcript presence.

Expected: Inventory: informative. 1.2.1/1.2.2: cantTell.

S16Embedded player + transcript link (explicit)

Iframe plus clearly labeled transcript link nearby.

Transcript

Expected: 1.2.1: possibly pass (strong transcript label evidence), even though player internals are unknown.

S17Video with audio hinted by nearby prose (“Audio included”)

Tests that you don’t treat prose as definitive proof.

Audio included.

Expected: 1.2.2: conservative result remains cantTell.

S18Video-only “alternative” via Description (not labeled transcript)

Alternative is arguably present but labeling is not explicit.

Description

A short description of what happens in the silent video.

Expected: 1.2.1: likely cantTell (not clearly an equivalent text alternative).

S19Transcript on separate URL (scanner does not crawl)

Simulates an external transcript page. Link is explicit.

Transcript

Expected: If the engine does not follow links: cantTell (cannot verify transcript content exists).

S20“Live” indicator (prerecorded applicability uncertain)

1.2.1/1.2.2 apply to prerecorded; “LIVE” here is not authoritative.

LIVE Stream

Expected: Typically cantTell on prerecorded vs live unless you have strong proof.

S21Audio-only with aria-controls pointing to transcript (IDREF association)

Not standard for transcript, but tests association signals beyond describedby.

A transcript is available below.

Transcript

[Transcript text] This transcript is associated via a UI control, not via describedby.

Expected: Conservative engines: cantTell unless you explicitly support this association pattern.

S22Video with captions track but mislabeled (caption kind wrong)

Track exists but uses a non-standard kind value.

Expected: 1.2.2: likely cantTell/informative (track present but kind invalid → not provably captions).

Notes for competitive analysis

  • Some tools treat any nearby long text as a transcript; this fixture includes counterexamples (S03, S14, S18).
  • Some tools only recognize the literal word “Transcript”; this fixture includes other patterns (aria-describedby, details, anchors).
  • Native <track kind="captions"> is widely detected; embedded players are often cantTell without provider logic.
  • Hidden transcript handling varies (S11). Decide a strict deterministic policy and standardize it.
  • If your engine does not crawl links, treat external transcript links (S19) as evidence but not proof.
